## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Nigamana* ("Epilogue"), designated as Mil 8, constitutes the terminal section of the post-canonical *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records three modern translations of this text across three languages [SuttaCentral]. None of the secondary literature passages located in the research corpus specifically discuss this concluding portion of the *Milindapañha*, as the matches for *nigamana* refer entirely to closing verses or colophons of other canonical and post-canonical works, or to the concluding statement (*nigamana*) within Indian syllogistic logic.

No cross-language parallels are cataloged on SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus with a score of 10 or higher [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus does, however, record Pali-internal text reuse comprising 44 matches across three texts [DharmaNexus]. The text shares extensive material with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), including 34 matching passages (2,179 characters; longest match §4.1_3 ↔ §1635_15) in the first volume and 5 matches (327 characters) in the second volume [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, 5 passages (332 characters) are shared with the *Catukkanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4), with the longest correspondence found between §3.2_2–3.2_3 and AN 4.111 (§111.5.3) at a similarity score of 0.86 [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
